public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Convergence of the Borwein Series with Sinusoidal Coefficient

*References:*
- [MathWorld, Harmonic Series](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/HarmonicSeries.html)
- Borwein, J.; Bailey, D.; Girgensohn, R. *Experimentation in Mathematics: Computational Paths
  to Discovery*, A K Peters, 2004, p. 56.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace BorweinSineSeries

/--
Does the series
$$
  \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\left(\frac{2}{3} + \frac{1}{3}\sin n\right)^n}{n}
$$
converge?

After computing approximately $10^7$ terms, the partial sums approximate $2.163$.

See https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.11017 for a proof of the convergence,
relying on an irrationality measure for pi.

Also see
https://github.com/AxiomMath/gdm-formal-conjectures/blob/main/docs/BorweinSineSeries.md
for a partial formalization of the conjecture,
conditional on such an irrationality measure of pi (cf https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.06345).
-/
@[category research solved, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/AxiomMath/gdm-formal-conjectures/blob/main/BorweinSineSeries/solution.lean",  AMS 26 40]
theorem borwein_sine_series :
    answer(True) ↔
      Summable fun n : ℕ+ ↦ ((2 / 3 + 1 / 3 * Real.sin (n : ℝ)) ^ (n : ℕ)) / (n : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end BorweinSineSeries

status_issues.recorded: @[category research solved, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/AxiomMath/gdm-formal-conjectures/blob/main/BorweinSineSeries/solution.lean"]: an unconditional record claiming the statement is formally proved in Lean 4.
status_issues.source_status: The linked Lean proof is conditional. Its main theorem is `theorem borwein_sine_series (hpi : PiIrrBound) : Summable fun n : ℕ+ ↦ ((2 / 3 + 1 / 3 * Real.sin (n : ℝ)) ^ (n : ℕ)) / (n : ℝ)`. Here `PiIrrBound := ∃ (C : ℝ) (Q₀ : ℕ), 0 < C ∧ ∀ (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ), 0 < q → Q₀ ≤ q → C / (q : ℝ) ^ muPi < |π - p / q|` with `muPi := 7.10321`. This is an irrationality-measure bound for π that neither the linked file nor Mathlib proves. Mathematically it is true: Zeilberger–Zudilin 2020 show μ(π) ≤ 7.103205334…. The problem itself is settled unconditionally by Boppana, arXiv:2007.11017, so the category and `answer(True)` are correct. Only the formal-proof record overstates what exists.
status_issues.evidence: (1) The linked solution.lean, fetched raw from main, ends with `theorem borwein_sine_series (hpi : PiIrrBound) : Summable …`. I compiled it against this checkout's Mathlib. One `simp at h` (line 425) needed a `try` because of a Mathlib version difference. After that, `#check` gives `PiIrrBound → Summable fun n => …` and `#print axioms` gives only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. So the proof is sorry-free but takes the assumption as a parameter. In a scratch file I checked that the linked statement yields the repository statement only when `hpi : PiIrrBound` is supplied. (2) AxiomMath's docs/BorweinSineSeries.md, which the file cites, says: "We provided this problem to AxiomProver as a test case, without referencing Boppana's paper, but including an assumption on the irrationality measure of pi." (3) The file's own docstring calls the link "a partial formalization of the conjecture, conditional on such an irrationality measure of pi". (4) At this commit, FormalConjecturesUtil/Attributes/Basic.lean documents the `conditional` modifier for exactly this case: "the proof at the link establishes the statement only under hypotheses the author has not proved … `#print axioms` on a proof that takes its assumption as a parameter comes back clean, so it has to be written down". The `lean4` kind means "The problem is solved in Lean 4 …, perhaps as an equivalent statement". PROOFS.md also requires checking "that the linked statement implies the repository statement". (5) Repository practice agrees: erdos_694 and erdos_659 have conditional Lean formalizations, mention them only in the docstring, and carry no `formal_proof` attribute.
status_issues.suggested_change: Option 1: add the hypothesis to the file as a `sorry` declaration and mark the proof conditional, keeping `research solved` and `answer(True)`. Use a commit-pinned link. For example: `/-- Zeilberger–Zudilin (2020): μ(π) ≤ 7.103205334…; in particular … -/ @[category research solved, AMS 11] theorem pi_irrationality_measure : ∃ (C : ℝ) (Q₀ : ℕ), 0 < C ∧ ∀ (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ), 0 < q → Q₀ ≤ q → C / (q : ℝ) ^ (7.10321 : ℝ) < |Real.pi - (p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)| := by sorry`, then `@[category research solved, conditional formal_proof using lean4 at "<pinned link>" assuming pi_irrationality_measure, AMS 26 40]`. Option 2: drop the `formal_proof` attribute and keep the docstring's description of the conditional formalization, as erdos_694 and erdos_659 do.

reformulations.difference: The source asks whether the series ∑_{n≥1} (2/3 + (1/3) sin n)^n / n converges, meaning its partial sums converge. The Lean statement uses `Summable` over `ℕ+`, which is unconditional summability (`SummationFilter.unconditional PNat`). The repository itself notes, for Erdős 15, that the two notions can differ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every real x, 2/3 + (1/3) sin x lies in [1/3, 1], so every term is positive (and at most 1/n). For nonnegative real terms, unconditional summability is equivalent to convergence of the partial sums (`hasSum_iff_tendsto_nat_of_nonneg`). The bijection ℕ+ ≃ ℕ, n ↦ n − 1 (`Equiv.pnatEquivNat`), turns the ℕ+ sum into ∑_{i<N} f(i+1) = ∑_{n=1}^N f(n). Also, `answer(True)` elaborates to `True`, so the theorem is just the right-hand side. I proved in Lean, with only the standard axioms, both `(Summable fun n : ℕ+ ↦ …) ↔ ∃ L, Tendsto (fun N ↦ ∑ i ∈ range N, bterm (i+1)) atTop (𝓝 L)` and `type_of% borwein_sine_series ↔ ∃ L, Tendsto (…) atTop (𝓝 L)`, where `bterm n = (2/3 + 1/3 * sin n)^n / n`.

review.notes: No mathematical findings. The theorem states exactly the question of Borwein–Bailey–Girgensohn (p. 56) as quoted by MathWorld and by Boppana. From `pp.explicit`: numerals are real, `1 / 3 * sin n` parses as (1/3)·sin n, sin takes n in radians, the power is a natural-number power, the division is by n ≥ 1 (no x/0 case), and `Summable` uses the unconditional filter over ℕ+, which matches ∑_{n=1}^∞. The terms are positive, so this is the source's notion of convergence; that equivalence is proved in Lean and recorded under reformulations. `answer(True)` and `research solved` are correct. I read Boppana's proof and it is complete and unconditional. Its only Diophantine input is the classical bound |π − p/q| > q^{-20} (Chudnovsky, or Mahler with exponent 42). The cited MathWorld page still says the question is open, but it predates that proof; this is not a defect of the file. Numerically, Lean Float gives partial sums of 2.1195 (N=10^3), 2.1588 (N=10^5), 2.1618 (N=10^6) and 2.16276 (N=10^7), which supports the docstring's '≈ 2.163'. The only defect is metadata, reported under status_issues: the unconditional `formal_proof using lean4` points to a proof of `PiIrrBound → Summable …`. Minor points: the formal_proof link targets `blob/main` rather than a commit, while PROOFS.md asks for a stable link (117 other links in the repository do the same). The linked solution.lean needed one `simp at h` → `try simp at h` to compile under this checkout's Mathlib; it was produced with Lean 4.28.0. I could not open the book itself, and the AoPS thread cited by Boppana was blocked. Both secondary sources quote the same series and page, so I consider the statement settled. I did not follow the AxiomMath doc's link to the formal-conjectures documentation site.
